key: Lo! We offered the trust unto the heavens and the earth and the hills, but they shrank from bearing it and were afraid of it. And man assumed it.
s: Near the surah’s close, after the believers are told to speak straight, the ayah turns to the burden man took on; al-Tabari, on 33:72, reads the trust as every trust of religion and of people, since God confined it to no one kind.

evidence.words: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ما قاله الذين قالوا: إنه عُنِي بالأمانة في هذا الموضع: جميع معاني الأمانات في الدين وأمانات الناس وذلك أن الله لم يخص بقوله ﴿عَرَضْنَا الأمَانَةَ﴾ بعض معاني الأمانات لما وصفنا.
evidence.gloss: The most correct of the sayings on this is that of those who said that by the trust in this place is meant every sense of the trusts in religion and the trusts of people; for God did not, in His saying “We offered the trust”, single out some of the senses of trusts, for the reason we have described.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Ahzab 33:72, at 3604; it stops before “Lo! he hath proved a tyrant and a fool”, whole sentences). In his comment on 33:72 al-Tabari reports three readings of the trust (the duties and obedience of religion, from Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Qatada; the trusts of people, from Ibn Mas’ud; Adam entrusting his family to Qabil, from al-Suddi) and then in his own voice prefers every sense of trust in religion and among people, because God did not single out one kind. The reading paraphrases that exactly. CHANGED the context clause only: “after warnings to the hypocrites” pointed to 33:60 to 33:61, eleven ayahs back; the ayahs directly before 33:72 (33:70 to 33:71) tell the believers to guard their duty and speak straight, so the clause now says that. 43 words; entry-check ok.
